title: Asset Consistency
author: gago8D
selftext:
I’m working on a card game and need artwork for around 250 cards. I already have a handful of mockups that show the art style and overall look I’m going for.

I’ve got Claude cooking up a prompt right now, but what tool would you guys recommend for a project this size? My biggest priority is keeping the artwork consistent across the cards, with as few weird errors as possible. I know that’s easier said than done.

Normally I’d use ChatGPT or Nano Banana, but I’m a little worried about the style drifting over 250 cards, even if I do them in batches of 10–20.

Anyone tackled something similar? Would love suggestions for tools or workflows that worked for you.

comments.author: because-potato
comments.body: Include images of previous cards when generating them and prompt the generator to keep the art style consistent. It’ll wander a little bit, but that’s how I had the best luck generating matching assets.

comments.author: Significant-Neck-520
comments.body: I got a consistent art style from gemini by requesting with the same prompt copy and pasted, and requesting it to be like an oil painting masterpiece (old trick, still works). It would mostly be the style that gemini chose for it, but there was consistency (no need to keep the same session, the prompt was enough)

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: I have had a similar ish issue and as other people have said just be sure Claude or gpt or whoever can access your prior assets, give example, with Claude it has a very detailed MD going over the stylistic direction as well as things to do or not to do with my game

comments.author: yaosio
comments.body: Have it make the artwork programmatically.

comments.author: mannew2026
comments.body: I'm using sol for cards. The important thing is to get a consistent style name it and it's usually pretty good about being consistent after you reject some bad passes. Just keep it all in the same chat and take a look over the cards you don't like

replies.author: gago8D
replies.body: have you found that sol is better than astra? and also do you normally generate one card at a time or get it done in batches?

replies.author: mannew2026
replies.body: One at a time. Never in batches. Sol is cheaper than astra in tokens. And cards don't require enough work that the extra tokens would be worth it

replies.author: gago8D
replies.body: Makes sense I will give it a try.  I have a card template that green screens the card art.  I don't know if you run something similar but claude had suggested that I do that.

comments.author: algorys
comments.body:
Le mieux que j'ai utilisé c'est :

- Un prompt maitre
- + un prompt de la variation
- garder le même chat si possible (ça depend de la complexité de l'image)
- si tu gardes pas le mème chat, remettre une image "type" en même temps

comments.author: bigpapirick
comments.body: I use ChatGPT and with the right style doc and examples we have been very consistent over 150 images.

comments.author: Ok-Fennel6578
comments.body: Are the 250 cards mostly different subjects, or will the same characters appear across several cards?
